name: Generate a Semantic-Layer Data Product from a Schema

checks.check: The SemanticRegistry declares customer_profile with grain="CUSTOMER_ID" and order_event with grain="ORDER_ID".
total_revenue uses Agg.SUM on AMOUNT_USD; order_count uses Agg.COUNT_DISTINCT on ORDER_ID.
churned_customer_count and first_order_count set boolean=True so the compiler emits a boolean CASE-sum rather than a numeric cast, instead of treating the flag column as a numeric SUM.
The join from order_event to customer_profile is declared with cardinality many_to_one (Cardinality.MANY_TO_ONE).
The EMAIL and FULL_NAME dimensions are registered with pii=True, and no other dimension is marked pii=True.

The agent vendored the experimental/semantic kit (copied compile_selection / build_semantic_tools) into the project rather than hand-writing compile_selection or the filter/aggregation logic. The DP's registry module contains only SemanticRegistry authoring and imports the compiler + tool factory from the kit.

The spec.py registers the four tool functions returned by build_semantic_tools(registry) as MCP-exposed tools via data_product_rpc_output()/rpc_function/rpc_server().mcp_path("/mcp") — not via a non-existent module-level tools list.
The project's dependency file (requirements.txt or pyproject.toml) lists the kit package / vendored path and any transitive requirements the kit declares.
The run_semantic_query tool handler contains no hand-written SQL strings; it delegates to compile_selection from the kit.
